Since $x>3,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & >3 \\ x-1 & >2 \\ |x-1| & >2 \\ |x-1|-1 & >1\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $|x-1|-1$ is positive for all the values of $x$ that we are considering $(x>3).$ So, we can multiply both sides by $|x-1|-1,$ and solve the resulting inequality as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8-2x}{|x-1|-1} & \ge 0 \\ (|x-1|-1)\cdot \frac{8-2x}{|x-1|-1} & \ge (|x-1|-1)\cdot 0 \\ 8-2x & \ge 0 \\ -2x & \ge -8 \\ x & \le 4\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we had to flip the sign of the inequality again since we divided by a negative number ($-2$).

Therefore, the solution to the inequality will be the numbers that satisfy both $x>3$ and $x\le 4.$ So, the solution to our inequality is

$$
3<x\le 4.
$$
